provenance.changes: Trimmed to one task and a few native records. Calibration tasks are explicitly narrowed exercises derived from that task; their answers and planted defects are hand-authored test data, not accepted production outcomes.

company.name: Clearwater Protection Systems — fictional analogue
company.operations: SEL designs and manufactures digital protection, automation and control equipment. Its captured About page identifies Pullman headquarters and US manufacturing since 1984. Captured support materials establish product-security assessment, code review and testing, continuing security updates and application engineering support. Clearwater models a bounded US sustaining-firmware and product-assurance unit within an established protective-relay manufacturer. It maintains shipped firmware, investigates defects, reviews remedies and prepares guidance for customers operating installed equipment. Synthetic scale: 24 employees support four relay families, twelve maintained firmware branches, approximately 180 US customer organizations and 14,000 registered devices. Ordinary monthly work includes 45 firmware/application support cases, eight escalated engineering investigations, three security assessments and two maintenance-candidate reviews; these categories overlap. A ten-year archive contains release notes, compatibility decisions, completed test reports and customer cases. The six listed workers are recurring decision participants, not the whole workforce. Their outputs include source analyses, verification assessments, remediation priorities, maintenance commitments and internally approved customer guidance. Manufacturing, laboratory execution, firmware signing and customer installation remain outside the selected digital cycles.

workers.title: Sustaining Software Manager
workers.responsibility: Receives the objective, creates the work plan, coordinates specialists, resolves competing priorities and integrates remediation or customer-guidance decisions. Manages the continuing firmware-maintenance portfolio.
information_access: Shared correspondence, documents, chat and calendar
Repository snapshots, engineering issues and review comments
Approved maintenance capacity and existing commitments
workers.authority: May allocate documented unit capacity and approve internal dispositions and guidance packages. Cannot replace missing technical evidence with managerial approval, authorize customer switching operations or certify unperformed tests.

workers.title: Embedded Firmware Developer
workers.responsibility: Traces behavior through source snapshots and branch configurations, reviews candidate code, evaluates reuse and backport feasibility, and defines correction requirements and acceptance criteria.
information_access: Branch-associated source files and build manifests
Candidate pull request descriptions and code snapshots
Defect reports, completed tests and change history
workers.authority: Owns software analysis and recommends accepting, revising or rejecting candidate changes. May update issues and review comments; an administrative merge or passing-check label cannot establish a working firmware image.

workers.title: Product Security Analyst
workers.responsibility: Evaluates attack prerequisites, affected scope and uncertainty; distinguishes confirmed vulnerabilities from unsupported reports; assesses mitigations, deferral exposure and candidate-change security implications.
information_access: Security intake reports and existing reproduction evidence
Internal disclosure rules and prior dispositions
workers.authority: Issues security assessments and recommends urgency and disclosure scope. May challenge unsupported risk reductions; the manager authorizes internal resource commitments and integrated packages.

workers.title: Protection Applications Engineer
workers.responsibility: Interprets protection requirements, hardware applicability and recorded customer configurations. Evaluates operational consequences of mitigations, firmware changes, rollback and maintenance deferral.
information_access: Existing event analyses and customer operating constraints
workers.authority: Defines supported application boundaries and identifies unsuitable mitigations. May recommend customer options but cannot approve a customer's outage, settings change or installation.

issues.title: Bound parser input and define frame ownership
issues.description:
Parser length and ownership changes require engineering preparation and review. Candidate C-PC is available for review; no completed candidate test report exists. Requirements R-PARSE-03, R-PARSE-04 and R-LIFE-02 apply. Scope includes length validation, interface and boundary harness. No window capacity has been assigned.

Support case: CS-26127. Work package: PK-SHARED. Dependencies: none.

issues.title: Adapt F400 4.8 service to parser correction
issues.description:
Engineering completion is required by September 14 under priority policy v2. Preserve remote event and settings functions and reject malformed frames. Review all caller and lifetime surfaces in F48-260717. Hardware D1/D2 acceptance remains required. Capacity has not been scheduled.

Support case: CS-26127. Work package: PK-MODERN. Depends on PK-SHARED, f400 #401.

issues.title: Adapt F400 4.2 maintenance parser
issues.description:
Assess the correction against the legacy allocator and callback requirements. B1/B2 compatibility and delayed payload consumption need acceptance evidence. Existing management-network restrictions remain in effect. No maintenance window is selected; responsible role is Embedded Firmware Developer.

Support case: CS-26129. Work package: PK-LEGACY. Depends on PK-SHARED, f400 #401.
